accepted.question: You have reserved cards showing a total of eight prestige points and two white bonuses, but have not bought them. Do those printed points count toward your score or the 15-point trigger, and do those bonuses reduce purchase costs or satisfy nobles?
accepted.reason: Distinguishes reserved-card state from acquired-card state for scoring and bonuses, not merely the tiebreaker exclusion in Q20.

accepted.question: You buy a development card with a blue bonus and zero prestige. Do you receive a physical blue token from the supply, does its bonus work for future purchases, and can it help qualify you for a noble despite being worth zero prestige?
accepted.reason: Tests zero-point developments and the distinction between a discount and generating physical currency.

accepted.question: A face-up development costs one blue and grants a blue bonus. You have no blue bonus, no blue token and no gold. Can its own bonus make this purchase free? Separately, suppose you can pay for a white-bonus development and it gives you the final bonus needed by a noble: does that new bonus count for the noble at the end of this turn, or only next turn?
accepted.reason: Contrasts two timing boundaries for a newly acquired bonus: paying for itself versus same-turn noble qualification.

accepted.question: A card costs one blue and two green. You have four blue bonuses and no green bonuses. Can the three excess blue bonuses pay any green cost or give you blue tokens as change? What payment is still needed?
accepted.reason: Tests colored discounts exceeding a cost and cross-color leakage, rather than just exact or fully covered costs.

accepted.question: You qualify for two nobles and receive one. Before your next turn nobody acquires the other noble and your purchased cards stay unchanged. Were the bonuses used up by the first noble, and can taking gems on your next turn still lead to receiving the other noble? Can you collect that other noble during an opponent’s intervening turn?
accepted.reason: Tests persistent eligibility across turns and checking after a non-purchase action, including the off-turn boundary.

accepted.question: You have no tokens, no purchased developments and no reserved cards. A face-up level-3 development is far too expensive for you to buy. May you reserve it anyway? Do you pay its printed cost when reserving, and do you take gold if available?
accepted.reason: Tests reserve affordability and level access independently of the purchase action.

accepted.question: Instead of reserving a face-up card, you reserve the top card of the level-2 deck while twelve face-up market cards remain. Must any market card be removed or refilled because of that blind reservation, how many market cards remain, and can you take a second card as a replacement in your hand?
accepted.reason: Tests the replacement trigger for a blind draw, distinct from face-up reservation and hand purchase.

accepted.question: A level deck has run out, but its four face-up cards are still in the market. Must those cards be removed, or may they still be purchased or reserved? If one is purchased, what happens to that space and to the other three cards?
accepted.reason: Tests the deck-exhaustion transition without discarding or disabling the remaining market.

accepted.question: All development decks and face-up market cards have been exhausted; nobody has reached fifteen prestige. A player still has an affordable reserved card and gems are available in at least three colors. Does exhaustion itself end the game? May that player buy the reserved card or choose the three-different-gems action?
accepted.reason: Tests global depletion versus the end condition and continued use of remaining legal actions.

accepted.question: You already own ten tokens. Three different gem colors are available. Can you take one of each and then return all three newly taken tokens, ending with exactly the same token holdings? Is a net gain of tokens required?
accepted.reason: Tests the zero-net-gain boundary, rather than returning only part of a draw.

accepted.question: The gold supply is empty. On A’s turn, A pays two gold while purchasing a card. B then reserves a card with fewer than three cards reserved. Are A’s spent gold tokens removed from the game, or can B take one, and how many gold tokens are left in the supply immediately after B’s reservation before any token-limit returns?
accepted.reason: Tests circulation of spent gold into the next player’s reserve action, not just the spent-token destination.

accepted.question: You have bought no level-1 or level-2 developments, but can pay for a face-up level-3 card. May you purchase that level-3 card now, or must you unlock its level by buying lower-level cards first?
accepted.reason: Tests purchase access to higher levels without a progression requirement.

accepted.question: You have twelve prestige, then purchase a three-prestige development whose bonus also makes you qualify for a noble. May you stop at fifteen and skip the noble visit? What is your total after your turn, and can the other players who still have a turn in the round continue playing?
accepted.reason: Tests completing mandatory end-of-turn resolution after the threshold is crossed by a purchase.

accepted.question: Four players act A, B, C, D, with A first. D is the first player to reach fifteen prestige on D’s turn. Does A start another round, does everyone get one more turn, or is the game over after D completes this turn? Explain using equal turn counts.
accepted.reason: Tests the last-player boundary of finish-current-round, not a trigger in the middle of a round.

accepted.question: In a two-player game, three nobles were revealed and the other seven removed during setup. After someone receives one noble, do you reveal a new tile from those seven to restore the display to three? Where does the acquired tile go and how many nobles remain available in the middle?
accepted.reason: Tests noble-display depletion versus development-market replenishment.

accepted.question: Match each component name to its color: emerald, diamond, sapphire, onyx, ruby and gold joker. How many development cards are in the box in total and at each of the three levels?
accepted.reason: Adds source component identities and development inventory counts not requested by the original setup questions.

accepted.question: A card’s remaining cost after bonuses is one green. You hold both one green token and one gold. Must you spend green because you have it, or may you pay gold instead and keep the green? Where does the payment go?
accepted.reason: Tests optional wildcard substitution when a matching ordinary gem is available; prior wildcard question covered missing-color payment only.

accepted.question: Three gem piles contain one red, two blue and three green tokens. Other gem piles are empty. Can the three-different-gems action take one from each of these piles, or does the four-token minimum prohibit it? What would remain in those three piles?
accepted.reason: Tests the other branch of the four-token condition: single tokens from sparse piles, not only the two-alike action.

accepted.question: You hold a gold token and want to exchange it directly for a red token in the supply without buying a development. Is that a listed action or a permitted use of the joker rule? What use does the summary give gold when purchasing?
accepted.reason: Tests payment substitution versus converting physical tokens as a standalone action.

accepted.question: On your turn you can legally buy a face-up card and can also take three different gems. You want neither benefit. May you simply pass without performing an action, or must you choose one of the four actions? This asks about voluntarily passing with legal actions available, not a state in which all actions are impossible.
accepted.reason: Tests zero actions versus mandatory one action; original question tested combining two actions. All-actions-impossible handling remains outside source scope.

accepted.question: During setup, how should the gem and gold supply be arranged: are all tokens mixed together or sorted, how many distinct piles are made, and where should they be placed relative to players?
accepted.reason: Source-rule inventory found setup supply arrangement not directly requested before; earlier questions assumed colored piles but did not test six sorted accessible piles.

accepted.question: At the end of the final round you have twelve prestige printed on purchased developments, one acquired noble, four unspent gold and five other gem tokens. What is your final prestige score? Do leftover gold or gem tokens add points?
accepted.reason: Source-rule inventory found the resource-versus-score boundary: prior scoring scenarios excluded reserved cards, but did not test unused tokens as proposed prestige.
